about: The Common Preface names no mystery of the day. After “through Christ our Lord” it turns to the angelic choirs' praise of God. Its opening sentence is built around “est”, which governs the construction “nos tibi grátias ágere”.

seg.nr: The priest parts his hands and holds them apart to the end of the Preface.

seg.tr: Truly it is right and just, fitting and leading to salvation, that we should give You thanks always and everywhere:

fn.w002: “Vere dignum et iustum est” takes up the answer “Dignum et iustum est”.
fn.w005: The only finite verb in this sentence. Its subject is the construction “nos tibi grátias ágere”.
fn.w008: Neuter singular of salutáris, in a series with dignum, iustum and æquum. Here it is the adjective “salutary”.
fn.w009: The accusative subject of the infinitive “ágere” (w015) — a construction English renders with a that-clause.
fn.w015: The infinitive in “nos tibi grátias ágere”, a construction governed by “est” (w005).

seg.tr: Holy Lord, almighty Father, eternal God: through Christ our Lord.

fn.w025: At this point the proper prefaces insert a section referring to the day or mystery.

seg.tr: Through Him the Angels praise Your majesty, the Dominions adore it, and the Powers tremble before it.

fn.w027: A relative pronoun referring to Christ.
fn.w028: One object for three verbs: they praise it, adore it, tremble before it.

seg.tr: The heavens, the heavenly Virtues, and the blessed Seraphim join in joyful celebration of Your majesty.

fn.w037: A genitive depending on “Virtútes” (w038): the Virtues belonging to the heavens.
fn.w042: An ablative of manner with “exsultatióne” (w043), not a nominative with the subjects.
fn.w044: The subjects are the angelic choirs: the verb describes their shared praise.

seg.tr: We beseech You to admit our voices to join theirs as we speak in humble confession:

fn.w046: Ablative after “cum”, referring to the angelic choirs.
fn.w049: The accusative subject of the infinitive “admítti” (w051) — “iúbeas” (w052) governs the whole construction.
fn.w052: A subjunctive after ut. The petition is put as a wish rather than a command.
fn.w053: A deponent: passive in form, active in meaning.
fn.w055: A confession not of guilt but of praise — what the Sanctus is about to sing.
fn.w056: The participle agrees with the unstated “we” and introduces the Sanctus.
